title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（辰巳仁史研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Tatsumi Hitoshi)
educationalGoal: Dynamic reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton is crucial for a number of cellular processes including cytokinesis, cell motility, and morphogenesis.
advice: Students will attend lectures introducing several research concepts. Dynamic reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton is crucial for a number of cellular processes including cytokinesis, cell motility, and morphogenesis. However, filamentous actin alone is relatively stable, and acceleration of filament disassembly is often required to promote actin cytoskeletal dynamics. ADF/cofilin is one of the major factors to accelerate disassembly of actin filaments by enhancing filament fragmentation and monomer dissociation from the pointed end. However, in vitro studies indicate that ADF/cofilin alone severs actin filaments only weakly and optimally when a cluster of ADF/cofilin molecules bind to an actin filament at low densities. When ADF/cofilin binds to the side of actin filaments at high densities, fragmentation of the filaments is rather infrequent. These biochemical properties suggest that ADF/cofilin alone may not be sufficient to account for rapid turnover of actin filaments observed in live cells. ADF/cofilin is one of the major factors to accelerate disassembly of actin filaments by enhancing filament fragmentation. Tension dependent changes in actin filament fluctuations, and ADF/cofilin molecules bind to an actin filament. It is possible that a mechano-dependent process is involvement in cell re-organization.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry. High school-level knowledge of biology. Students should have learned basic cell biology.
